title: A birthday party, not a second job
request: Create one 30-second vertical TikTok for busy parents: decoration and message chaos, parent says 'It’s a birthday party, not a second job.', shares Envitefy invitation, guests RSVP and Add to Calendar with confirmations, parent relaxes until child says 'Actually, I want a different theme.' End 'Less planning. More partying. Envitefy.com.' Realistic people, quick cuts, playful music, readable captions.
audience: Busy parents planning children's birthday parties
objective: Show the relief of one invitation link with RSVP and calendar actions, with a relatable parenting punchline.
concept: Dinosaur party admin overwhelms Dad. One Envitefy link handles guest logistics. His child requests a new theme just as he sits down.
tone: Observational parenting comedy; affectionate, dry delivery

artDirection.cast: Fictional dad, about 38, short dark hair with grey at temples, short beard, warm brown skin; his fictional seven-year-old daughter with curly dark ponytail; two adult guests in separate homes.
artDirection.setting: Modest sunlit suburban kitchen/dining room, sage cabinetry, pale wood table, green and orange dinosaur party decorations
artDirection.wardrobe: Dad wears a faded rust-orange crew-neck T-shirt and jeans; child wears lilac overalls and a white T-shirt
artDirection.visualTreatment: Candid realistic live-action motion, quick hard cuts, human skin texture, natural dialogue, bold editable captions
artDirection.continuityNotes: Payoff generation references the first dad clip. No still-photo storytelling.
artDirection.differenceFromRecentCampaigns: New male parent, family setting, rust wardrobe, dinosaur birthday, spoken comedy instead of the Host Mode house party

shots.chaos: Generate exactly 10 seconds of vertical 9:16 realistic live action parenting comedy with synchronized natural spoken dialogue. Modest sunny suburban kitchen, sage cabinets, pale wood dining table. Dinosaur birthday preparation has taken over: green and orange balloons, green paper streamers draped over his shoulder, cardboard dinosaurs, party hats, unfilled goodie bags. [0-1.6s] Medium wide shot: he struggles with a tangled streamer while a green balloon escapes behind him. [1.6-3s] Quick cut to closeup of his face reacting to successive phone buzzes; he is holding a black smartphone in one hand, the screen facing him, screen not readable. [3-4s] Cut to waist-up as another strip of paper clings to his forearm; he pauses and looks directly into the lens. [4-8s] Closeup of face, holds eye contact, dry exhausted natural American English delivery, clearly says exactly: 'It’s a birthday party, not a second job.' Understated authentic comedic acting, accurate lip sync, normal conversational pace, no extra words. Keep eyes in upper-middle frame, leave bottom third for captions. No rendered text, no subtitles, no logos, no music. Audio: quiet kitchen ambience, three short generic message buzzes before speech, clean intelligible dialogue, gentle handling sound. No extra people or voices.

shots.payoff: Generate a NEW exactly 10-second vertical 9:16 realistic live action sequel with the exact SAME dad identity, rust-orange T-shirt, grey-templed short hair, beard and the same sunny sage kitchen/dining room from the preceding reference video. The green and orange dinosaur decorations are now neatly arranged. Do not replay the previous clip. [0-2s] Medium shot: Dad settles into a chair, puts down his phone, exhales in relief, reclines with a mug held naturally in one hand. [2-3s] His seven-year-old daughter, fictional child with warm brown skin, dark curly ponytail, lilac overalls over white T-shirt, enters the frame from the side, relaxed and innocent. [3-6.5s] Cut to a medium two-shot showing daughter clearly. In a natural expressive child's American English voice she says EXACTLY: 'Actually, I want a different theme.' Dad is silent. Clear accurate lip sync and normal speech. [6.5-8s] Cut close to Dad, completely still deadpan stare into camera, slowly lowers his mug, one subtle eyebrow raise. [8-10s] He gives a tiny resigned smile and daughter happily skips out of frame. Natural believable parenting comedy; no exaggerated grimace. Consistent set, wardrobe and actor, ordinary handheld footage, faces upper-middle with lower third clear. Real moving footage, no frozen picture. Clean native synchronized child dialogue, gentle chair sound and quiet room ambience. No music, no narrator, no other words, no subtitles, no text, no logos.
